speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; I understand you have blood in your urine and pain on your right side. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me if the pain is severe enough to make you nauseous or if it radiates to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; since the pain radiates to the groin, do you notice any small, pebble-like particles passing in your urine, or have you had any fevers or chills recently?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy
REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture

text:
The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria and white blood cells, but the negative nitrites make a simple bacterial infection less likely. Given your history of recurrent infections and the specific finding of "pebble-like particles," have you noticed any difficulty starting your urine stream or a feeling of incomplete emptying?
